elements.element: IBM's liability cap must equal the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: IBM's cap is revised to “the greater of USD 1,000,000 or the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim related to the Services.”

elements.element: Customer's liability cap must equal the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Customer's cap remains the greater of $100,000 or charges paid in the 12 months preceding accrual of the first claim; it lacks the USD 1,000,000 floor, payable fees and the required claim trigger.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect damages must apply mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10 states that “either party” will not be liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: The exclusion of consequential damages must apply mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10 states that “either party” will not be liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of confidentiality obligations must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually defines breach of confidentiality obligations as Excluded Claims and states that Section 9's limitations do not apply.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of data protection obligations must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually defines breach of data protection obligations as Excluded Claims and states that Section 9's limitations do not apply.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of security obligations must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually defines breach of security obligations as Excluded Claims and states that Section 9's limitations do not apply.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 includes “a party's indemnification obligations under Section 8” as Excluded Claims outside Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for gross negligence must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 includes each party's gross negligence as an Excluded Claim outside Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for wilful misconduct must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 includes each party's wilful misconduct as an Excluded Claim outside Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for fraud must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 includes each party's fraud as an Excluded Claim outside Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights must be uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 includes “a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights” as an Excluded Claim outside Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations must not constitute damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 expressly states that “Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not damages for purposes of the limitations in this Section 9.”

elements.element: IBM's liability cap must equal 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: IBM's cap is the greater of USD 1,000,000 or 12 months' paid or payable fees, so it does not equal an unqualified 12-month-fees cap.

elements.element: Customer's liability cap must equal 12 months' fees on the same basis as IBM's cap.
elements.evidence: Customer's cap remains the greater of $100,000 or charges paid during a differently triggered 12-month period and therefore is neither a pure 12-month-fees cap nor mutual with IBM's cap.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations must be carved out from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually excludes each party's Section 8 indemnification obligations from Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for breach of confidentiality obligations must be carved out from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually excludes breach of confidentiality obligations from Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for gross negligence must be carved out from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually excludes gross negligence from Section 9's limitations.

elements.element: Each party's liability for wilful misconduct must be carved out from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 9.3 mutually excludes wilful misconduct from Section 9's limitations.

result.reason: The redline correctly revises IBM's cap, preserves the mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, adds all requested mutual uncapped carve-outs, and treats Customer payment obligations as non-damages. However, it expressly leaves Customer's materially different $100,000/paid-charges cap unchanged. The resulting caps are not mutual and satisfy neither the preferred formula nor the fallback 12-month-fees formula. The changes otherwise preserve unrelated terms and introduce no clear operative contradiction, but the redline is not minimal to a complete position because it reaches neither level.
